turns.assessment: The earliest and most localizing alarm is AMP_INPUT_LOS at the second amplifier on S04→S20, placing the hard loss between the S04 booster and amp1—span0. The simultaneous loss of many channels and services supports a common all-channel plant failure rather than a channel, client-port, WSS, or OTN-switch fault. Unchanged pump current argues against an amplifier pump failure. Although the reverse fibre remained normal, a one-direction fibre break is still the strongest explanation.

proposals.rationale: A break in oms.S04-S20.span0 would remove all optical input to amp1, exactly matching O1 and the simultaneous downstream OCH LOS and service failures. The unaffected reverse direction suggests only one fibre was broken rather than the usual whole cable cut.
A disconnected S04 OMS input patch would also remove every S04→S20 channel, but there was no recent maintenance at S04 and the alarm localization is compatible with a failure farther along at span0.
Failure of the upstream booster could produce amp1 input LOS, but amp0 pump current showed no change, which is evidence against pump failure.
A sufficiently large added loss on span0 could cross the detection threshold, but the abrupt, complete multi-channel LOS pattern is more consistent with a break.
